paragraphs: We are a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company developing product candidates that precisely target proteins that are critical to immune cell maturation and function. We believe our proprietary product candidates have broad potential to address immune mediated diseases, inflammatory diseases and cancers.

Our lead product candidate, soquelitinib (formerly CPI-818), is designed to bind specifically to a protein, interleukin 2 inducible T cell kinase (ITK), involved in T cell activation, T cell receptor signaling and T cell differentiation and function. Based on the proposed mechanism of action, we believe soquelitinib has the potential to be utilized to inhibit the production of a number of inflammatory cytokines involved in diseases such as atopic dermatitis, hidradenitis suppurativa, asthma, psoriasis and fibrotic diseases. In preclinical studies, Soquelitinib has affected T cell differentiation leading to enhanced function of T cells involved in tumor cell eradication.

Since the immune cells targeted by our product candidates play a role in many diseases, our strategy is to leverage our research and development capabilities by evaluating our product candidates in clinical trials where there is an understanding of the role of specific T cells in the target indication and where we believe such product candidates have the broadest potential. We believe this strategy has enabled us to move rapidly from preclinical to clinical trials in diverse disease areas, each with large unmet needs. Soquelitinib entered both a registrational, Phase 3 clinical trial for relapsed T cell lymphomas and a recently initiated randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial in patients with atopic dermatitis. We have two additional product candidates which are in clinical development for the treatment of various solid tumors, also based on modulation of immune function.
Our product candidate pipeline and anticipated milestones include the following:
(1) The Company did not conduct Phase 1 studies for these specific indications, but is planning to initiate Phase 2 studies for these indications based on the Phase 1 Atopic Dermatitis study.

Soquelitinib (CPI-818), ITK Inhibitor. Soquelitinib is an investigational selective, orally bioavailable, covalent inhibitor of ITK. ITK, an enzyme that functions in T cell signaling and differentiation, is expressed predominantly in T cells, which are lymphocytes that play a vital role in immune responses. T cell lymphomas are malignancies of T cells that proliferate and spread throughout the body. These lymphomas often have uncontrolled tonic signaling through the T cell receptor pathway, which involves ITK. Inhibition of ITK with soquelitinib could result in blockade of this signaling pathway and control the growth of the malignancy. In addition, one of the key survival mechanisms of both lymphomas

and solid tumors is believed to be the reprogramming of normal T cells to create an environment in the tissues that inhibits an anti-tumor immune response and favors tumor growth. We believe highly selective inhibitors of this enzyme will facilitate induction of normal T cell anti-tumor immunity and may be useful in the treatment of solid tumors as well as lymphomas. A normal functioning immune system maintains balance between inflammation, needed to fight infection or eliminate noxious agents, and suppression of inflammation necessary when the inflammatory signals are eliminated. This balance is restored through the action of T regulatory cells, which dampen inflammatory responses. ITK plays a vital role in the function of these regulatory T cells where it acts to modulate immune responses.

In ITK genetic knockout mice, which completely lack expression of ITK, T cells exhibit defects in T helper cell differentiation and cytokine secretion but retain the ability to differentiate into cytotoxic T cells that secrete IL-2 and interferon gamma ("IFNg"), which are the cells responsible for tumor rejection. We believe that skewing T helper cell differentiation to favor cytotoxic T cells, known as Th1 skewing, may be beneficial in treating T cell lymphomas and many other types of cancer. Mice with genetic knock-out of ITK also demonstrate a reduction in Th2 and Th17 cells, which produce the cytokines that are often responsible for autoimmunity and allergy such as interleukin (Il) Il-4, Il-5, Il-13, Il-17 and many others.

We have designed and developed soquelitinib to covalently target the cysteine amino acid residue at position 442 in the ITK protein. We believe this irreversible targeting of ITK has the potential to provide a potent, selective and prolonged duration of activity without the need for high systemic exposures and thereby improve the therapeutic window. This approach was previously used by our cofounders to generate ibrutinib. Selective inhibition of ITK can block the production and function of Th2 and Th17 helper T cells, potentially leading to a biasing toward the differentiation of naïve T cells into Th1 helper T cells. Th1 cells lead to the generation of killer T cells that can eliminate tumor cells or viral infected cells. Th1 cells produce interferon gamma and tumor necrosis factor that are cytokines known to destroy cancer cells. We believe, based on our preclinical and Phase 1/1b data from our T cell lymphoma clinical trial, that soquelitinib has the potential to reprogram normal immune responses that also could be beneficial for the treatment of certain autoimmune, inflammatory and allergic diseases. Overactive Th2 and Th17 cells are known to play a role in autoimmune, inflammatory and allergic diseases, which can potentially be ameliorated by selective ITK inhibition by blocking Th2 and Th17 function and their production of inflammatory cytokines such as IL4, IL5, IL13, IL17 and others.

In December 2024, we and our academic collaborators published results describing the chemistry, enzymology and preclinical anti-tumor activity of soquelitinib in the journal npj Drug Discovery. Key results from the publication include that soquelitinib:
● Selectively bound to and inhibited ITK function while sparing other closely related kinases, including resting lymphocyte kinase.

● Inhibited Th2 T cell function and the production of various Th2 cytokines leading to Th1 skewing and production of interferon gamma and tumor necrosis factor, which are important cytokines in tumor rejection. Th2 cytokines have been previously implicated in promoting tumor growth and are also involved in autoimmune and allergic diseases.
● Activated cytotoxic killer cells and increases infiltration of these cells into tumors.
● Reduced and reversed T cell exhaustion resulting in a more potent and prolonged immune response. T cell exhaustion is often a major reason for resistance to immune checkpoint therapy.

headings: Risks Related to Our Limited Operating History, Financial Condition and Need for Additional Capital
Risks Related to the Discovery and Development of Our Product Candidates
If we encounter difficulties enrolling subjects in our clinical trials, our clinical development activities could be delayed or otherwise adversely affected.
We may not be successful in our efforts to identify or discover additional product candidates.
Risks Related to Our Reliance on Third Parties
We rely on third parties to conduct some or all aspects of our manufacturing, research and preclinical and clinical testing, and these third parties may not perform satisfactorily.

We and our contract manufacturers are subject to significant regulation with respect to manufacturing our products and the contract manufacturers on which we rely may not continue to meet regulatory requirements.

Our reliance on third parties requires us to share our trade secrets, which increases the possibility that a competitor will discover them or that our trade secrets will be misappropriated or disclosed.
Risks Related to Commercialization of Our Product Candidates
If we do not achieve our projected development goals in the time frames we announce and expect, the commercialization of our products may be delayed and, as a result, our stock price may decline.
paragraphs: Our business involves significant risks, some of which are described below. You should consider carefully the risks and uncertainties described below, together with all of the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our audited consolidated financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations." If any of the following risks are realized, our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects could be materially and adversely affected. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also impair our business operations.

We have incurred significant operating losses since our inception and expect to incur significant losses for the foreseeable future. We may never generate any revenue or become profitable or, if we achieve profitability, we may not be able to sustain it.

We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company that has never generated revenue from the sale of our product candidates. Biopharmaceutical product development is a highly speculative undertaking and involves a substantial degree of risk. To date, we have focused primarily on developing our lead product candidates, soquelitinib, ciforadenant and mupadolimab, and researching additional product candidates. We have incurred significant operating losses since we were founded in January 2014 and have not yet generated any revenue from sales. If our product candidates are not approved, we may never generate any revenue. We incurred a net loss of $15.3 million, $62.3 million and $27.0 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. We had an accumulated deficit of $412.3 million as of December 31, 2025. We expect to continue to incur losses for the foreseeable future, and we anticipate these losses will increase as we continue our development of, seek regulatory approval for and, if approved, begin to commercialize soquelitinib, and as we develop other product candidates. Even if we achieve profitability in the future, we may not be able to sustain it in subsequent periods. Our prior losses, combined with expected future losses, have had and will continue to have an adverse effect on our stockholders' equity and results of operations.

We will require substantial additional financing to achieve our goals, and a failure to obtain this necessary capital when needed on acceptable terms, or at all, could force us to delay, limit, reduce or terminate our product development, other operations or commercialization efforts.

Since our inception, the majority of our efforts have been focused on the research and development of soquelitinib, ciforadenant and mupadolimab. We believe that we will continue to expend substantial resources for the foreseeable future as we continue clinical development of, seek regulatory approval for and, if approved, prepare for the commercialization of soquelitinib, as well as product candidates under our other development programs. These expenditures will include costs associated with research and development, conducting preclinical studies and clinical trials, obtaining regulatory approvals, manufacturing and supply, sales and marketing and general operations. In addition, other unanticipated costs may arise. Because the outcome of any clinical trial and/or regulatory approval process is highly uncertain, we may not be able to accurately estimate the actual amounts necessary to successfully complete the development, regulatory approval process and commercialization of soquelitinib, ciforadenant and mupadolimab or any other product candidates.

As of December 31, 2025, we had capital resources consisting of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $56.8 million. On January 23, 2026, we completed a follow-on offering of common stock, which resulted in aggregate net proceeds of approximately $189.4 million.

This Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the following sections, contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the federal securities laws. For a detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties, see the "Risk Factors" section in Item 1A of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. We caution the reader not to place undue reliance on these forward-looking statements, which reflect management's analysis only as of the date of this Form 10-K. We undertake no obligation to update forward-looking statements, which reflect events or circumstances occurring after the date of this Form 10-K.

We are a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company developing product candidates that precisely target proteins that are critical to immune cell maturation and function. We believe our proprietary product candidates have broad potential to address immune mediated diseases, inflammatory diseases and cancers.

Our lead product candidate, soquelitinib (formerly CPI-818), is designed to bind specifically to a protein, interleukin 2 inducible T cell kinase (ITK), involved in T cell activation, T cell receptor signaling and T cell differentiation and function. Based on the proposed mechanism of action, we believe soquelitinib has the potential to be utilized to inhibit the production of a number of inflammatory cytokines involved in diseases such as atopic dermatitis, hidradenitis suppurativa, asthma, psoriasis and fibrotic diseases. In preclinical studies, Soquelitinib has affected T cell differentiation leading to enhanced function of T cells involved in tumor cell eradication.

Since the immune cells targeted by our product candidates play a role in many diseases, our strategy is to leverage our research and development capabilities by evaluating our product candidates in clinical trials where there is an understanding of the role of specific T cells in the target indication and where we believe such product candidates have the broadest potential. We believe this strategy has enabled us to move rapidly from preclinical to clinical trials in diverse disease areas, each with large unmet needs. Soquelitinib entered a registrational, Phase 3 clinical trial for relapsed T cell lymphomas and is also being evaluated in a randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial in patients with atopic dermatitis. We have two additional product candidates which are in clinical development for the treatment of various solid tumors, also based on modulation of immune function.

To date, the majority of our efforts have been focused on the research, development and advancement of soquelitinib, ciforadenant, and mupadolimab, and we have not generated any revenue from product sales and, as a result, we have incurred significant losses. We expect to continue to incur significant research and development and general and administrative expenses related to our operations. Our net loss for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 was $15.3 million and $62.3 million, respectively, which includes non-operating income of $27.1 million and non-operating loss of $33.4 million, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $412.3 million. We expect our losses will increase as we continue our development of, seek regulatory approval for and begin to commercialize soquelitinib, ciforadenant and mupadolimab, and as we develop other product candidates. Even if we achieve profitability in the future, we may not be able to sustain profitability in subsequent periods.

Since our inception and through December 31, 2025, we have funded our operations primarily through the sale and issuance of stock, including through our initial public offering ("IPO") in March 2016 and subsequent follow-on public offerings. In May 2024, we completed a registered direct offering, in which we sold shares of our common stock, pre-funded warrants and common stock warrants for net proceeds of approximately $30.3 million and proceeds of $54.3 million from the exercise of common stock warrants.

On August 6, 2024, we entered into an open market sale agreement (the "2024 Sales Agreement") with Jefferies LLC ("Jefferies") to sell shares of our common stock, from time-to-time, with aggregate gross sales proceeds of up to $100.0 million, through an at-the-market equity offering program under which Jefferies will act as our sales agent. The issuance and sale of shares of common stock pursuant to the 2024 Sales Agreement are deemed an "at-the-market"

offering under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. Jefferies is entitled to compensation for its services of up to 3.0% of the gross proceeds of any shares of common stock sold through Jefferies under the 2024 Sales Agreement.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, we did not sell any shares of common stock under our at-the-market offering program and $100.0 million remained available for sale under the 2024 Sales Agreement.

In connection with the Company's follow-on public offering in January 2026, the Company suspended the "at-the-market" offering with respect to the 2024 Sales Agreement (See Footnote 17, Subsequent Event).

Our three product candidates, soquelitinib, ciforadenant and mupadolimab, are in clinical development by us and / or our partner, Angel Pharmaceuticals. Except for Greater China, we own the world-wide rights to these product candidates.

As a result of our ongoing development efforts, we anticipate needing to spend substantial resources for the foreseeable future. Consequently, we will need additional financing to support our continuing operations. Until such time as we can generate significant revenue from product sales, if ever, we expect to finance our operations through a combination of public or private equity or debt financings or other sources, which may include collaborations with third parties. Such financing could result in dilution to stockholders and may include the imposition of debt covenants and repayment obligations or other restrictions that may affect our business. If we raise additional capital through strategic collaboration agreements, we may have to relinquish valuable rights to our product candidates, including potential future revenue streams. Adequate additional financing may not be available to us on acceptable terms, or at all. For example, the trading prices for our and other biopharmaceutical companies' stock have been highly volatile as a result of factors such as the impacts of pandemics and increases in inflation rates or interest rates or the broad imposition of tariffs and other trade controls. As a result, we may face difficulties raising capital through sales of our common stock and any such sales may be on unfavorable terms. Our inability to raise capital as and when needed would have a negative impact on our financial condition and our ability to pursue our business strategy. We will need to generate significant revenue to achieve profitability, and we may never do so.

As of December 31, 2025, we had capital resources consisting of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of approximately $56.8 million and on January 23, 2026, we closed a follow-on public offering which resulted in aggregate net proceeds of approximately $189.4 million. Based on our currently available cash resources and our currently planned level of operations and cash flows, we expect that our cash resources will be sufficient to enable us to advance our programs into the second quarter of 2028. In accordance with applicable accounting standards, we evaluated whether there are conditions and events, considered in the aggregate, that raise substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern for at least the next 12 months from the date of the issuance of the consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and concluded that our existing cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, including the approximate net proceeds of $189.4 million from our January 2026 follow-on public offering, are sufficient to fund our operations for at least the next 12 months from issuance of the consolidated financial statements. However, the Company will need to continue to raise additional capital to fund its operations. See "Risk Factors—Risks Related to Our Limited Operating History, Financial Condition and Need for Additional Capital."

We currently have no manufacturing capabilities and do not intend to establish any such capabilities. We have no commercial manufacturing facilities for our product candidates. As such, we are dependent on third parties to supply our product candidates according to our specifications, in sufficient quantities, on time, in compliance with appropriate regulatory standards and at competitive prices.

paragraphs: 本公司為一家臨牀階段生技藥品公司，開發具體針對免疫細胞成熟與功能關鍵蛋白之產品候選藥物。本公司認為，本公司自有產品候選藥物具有廣泛潛力，可用以治療免疫介導疾病、發炎性疾病及癌症。

本公司主要產品候選藥物為 soquelitinib（原為 CPI-818），設計用以專門結合一種蛋白質，即 interleukin 2 inducible T cell kinase（ITK），此蛋白質參與 T 細胞活化、T 細胞受體訊號傳導及 T 細胞分化與功能。根據所提出的作用機制，本公司認為 soquelitinib 有潛力用以抑制參與如過敏性皮膚炎、hidradenitis suppurativa、氣喘、銀屑病及纖維化疾病等疾病之多種發炎性細胞激素之產生。在臨牀前研究中，soquelitinib 已影響 T 細胞分化，導致參與腫瘤細胞清除之 T 細胞功能增強。

由於本公司產品候選藥物所針對之免疫細胞在許多疾病中扮演角色，本公司策略為運用本公司研究與開發能力，評估產品候選藥物於臨牀試驗中，其中對目標適應症中特定 T 細胞之角色有明確理解，且本公司認為產品候選藥物具有最廣泛潛力之領域。本公司認為此策略已使本公司能快速從臨牀前階段轉入臨牀試驗，於各具大規模未滿足醫療需求之不同疾病領域。soquelitinib 已進入針對復發性 T 細胞淋巴瘤之註冊性第三期臨牀試驗，以及最近啟動之隨機安慰劑對照第二期臨牀試驗，用於治療過敏性皮膚炎之患者。本公司尚有兩種其他產品候選藥物正在臨牀開發中，用以治療各種實體腫瘤，亦基於免疫功能調節之概念。
本公司產品候選藥物管線及預期里程碑如下：
(1) 本公司未針對這些特定適應症進行第一期研究，但計畫根據第一期過敏性皮膚炎研究結果，啟動這些適應症的第二期研究。

Soquelitinib (CPI-818)，ITK 抑製劑。Soquelitinib 是一種正在研究中的選擇性、口服生物可利用、共價抑制 ITK 的藥物。ITK 是一種在 T 細胞訊號傳導與分化中發揮功能的酵素，主要在 T 細胞中表達，而 T 細胞是淋巴細胞，對免疫反應具有關鍵作用。T 細胞淋巴瘤是 T 細胞惡性增生並擴散至全身的癌症。這些淋巴瘤常見的生存機制之一為透過 T 細胞受體路徑的不受控制的持續訊號傳導，此過程涉及 ITK。以 Soquelitinib 抑制 ITK 可能會阻斷此訊號傳導路徑，並控制癌症的生長。此外，這兩種淋巴瘤的關鍵生存機制之一為

以及實體腫瘤的治療，認為這是將正常T細胞重新編程，以創造一種在組織中抑制抗腫瘤免疫反應並促進腫瘤生長的環境。我們認為，對此酵素的高選擇性抑制劑將有助於誘導正常T細胞的抗腫瘤免疫力，並可能在實體腫瘤以及淋巴瘤的治療中發揮作用。一個正常運作的免疫系統，維持炎症與抑制炎症之間的平衡，前者用以對抗感染或消除有害物質，後者則在炎症訊號消失時所需。這種平衡透過T調節細胞的作用來恢復，這些細胞會抑制炎症反應。ITK在這些調節T細胞的功能中扮演關鍵角色，它會調節免疫反應。

在ITK基因敲除小鼠中，這些小鼠完全缺乏ITK的表達，T細胞會在T輔助細胞分化和細胞激素分泌方面出現缺陷，但仍能分化為分泌IL-2和幹擾素伽馬（"IFNg"）的細胞毒性T細胞，這些細胞是負責腫瘤排斥的細胞。我們認為，將T輔助細胞分化傾向於細胞毒性T細胞，即所謂的Th1傾向，可能對治療T細胞淋巴瘤以及許多其他類型的癌症有益。具有ITK基因敲除的小鼠也顯示出Th2和Th17細胞的減少，這些細胞會產生常見於自身免疫和過敏反應的細胞激素，例如白血球介素（Il）Il-4、Il-5、Il-13、Il-17以及許多其他物質。

我們已設計並開發 soquelitinib 以共價作用於 ITK 蛋白質中第 442 個位置的半胱氨酸胺基酸殘基。我們認為這種不可逆的 ITK 作用方式有潛力提供強效、選擇性且持續時間較長的活性，而無需高系統性暴露，進而改善治療窗。此方法先前已由我們共同創辦人用於開發 ibrutinib。選擇性抑制 ITK 可阻斷 Th2 與 Th17 輔助 T 細胞的產生與功能，潛在導致 naïve T 細胞向 Th1 輔助 T 細胞分化偏移。Th1 細胞會產生殺手 T 細胞，這些細胞可消除腫瘤細胞或病毒感染的細胞。Th1 細胞產生幹擾素 gamma 與腫瘤壞死因子，這些細胞激素已知可破壞癌細胞。我們基於我們 T 細胞淋巴瘤臨牀試驗的預臨牀與 Phase 1/1b 資料，認為 soquelitinib 有潛力重新編程正常的免疫反應，這對某些自身免疫、發炎與過敏性疾病治療可能有益。過度活躍的 Th2 與 Th17 細胞已知在自身免疫、發炎與過敏性疾病中扮演角色，這些疾病可能透過選擇性 ITK 抑制，阻斷 Th2 與 Th17 功能及其產生發炎細胞激素（如 IL4、IL5、IL13、IL17 等）而得到改善。
2024 年 12 月，我們與學術合作夥伴發表了關於 soquelitinib 的化學、酵素學與預臨牀抗腫瘤活性的研究結果，刊登於 npj Drug Discovery 期刊。該研究的主要結果包括：
● 選擇性地與 ITK 作用並抑制其功能，同時不影響其他密切相關的絲氨酸/蘇氨酸蛋白激酶，包括靜息淋巴細胞激酶。
● 抑制 Th2 T 細胞功能與各種 Th2 細胞激素的產生，導致 Th1 偏移與幹擾素 gamma 與腫瘤壞死因子的產生，這些細胞激素在腫瘤排斥中至關重要。Th2 細胞激素先前已被認為促進腫瘤生長，同時也參與自身免疫與過敏性疾病。
● 激活細胞毒性殺手細胞並增加這些細胞進入腫瘤的浸潤。
● 減少並逆轉 T 細胞耗竭，導致更強效且持續時間更長的免疫反應。T 細胞耗竭通常是對免疫檢查點治療產生抗藥性的主要原因。

以下討論應配合本年度10-K表報表所附之合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。本年度10-K表報表，包括下列各節，包含根據聯邦證券法規所定義之向前看聲明。這些聲明受風險與不確定性影響，可能導致實際結果與事件與這些向前看聲明所表達或暗示者有重大差異。有關這些風險與不確定性的詳細討論，請參閱本年度10-K表報表第1A項之「風險因素」節。我們提醒讀者勿過度依賴這些向前看聲明，這些聲明僅反映管理階層於本10-K表報表日期之分析。我們不承擔更新向前看聲明之義務，這些聲明反映的是發生於本10-K表報表日期之後之事件或情況。
本公司為一臨牀階段生技藥品公司，開發具體針對免疫細胞成熟與功能關鍵蛋白之產品候選品。我們相信本公司專利產品候選品具有廣泛潛力，可用以對抗免疫介導疾病、發炎性疾病與癌症。

我們的首個產品候選品，soquelitinib（原為CPI-818），設計為專門結合一種蛋白質，即間質素2誘導T細胞激酶（ITK），此蛋白質參與T細胞活化、T細胞受體訊號傳導與T細胞分化與功能。根據所提出的機製作用，我們相信soquelitinib有潛力用以抑制參與如異位性皮膚炎、hidradenitis suppurativa、氣喘、銀屑病與纖維化疾病的多種發炎性細胞激素的產生。在臨牀前研究中，soquelitinib已影響T細胞分化，導致參與腫瘤細胞清除的T細胞功能增強。

由於我們產品候選品所針對的免疫細胞在許多疾病中扮演角色，我們的策略是利用我們的研究與開發能力，評估產品候選品在臨牀試驗中，其中對目標適應症中特定T細胞的角色有明確理解，且我們認為這些產品候選品具有最廣泛潛力。我們相信此策略使我們能快速從臨牀前階段轉入多種疾病領域的臨牀試驗，每個領域均有未滿足的重大需求。soquelitinib已進入針對復發性T細胞淋巴瘤的註冊性第三期臨牀試驗，同時也在進行一項隨機、安慰劑對照的第二期臨牀試驗，用於治療異位性皮膚炎患者。我們還有兩個額外的產品候選品正在臨牀開發中，用以治療各種實體腫瘤，同樣基於免疫功能的調節。

截至目前為止，本公司主要努力方向為研發及推進 soquelitinib、ciforadenant 與 mupadolimab 的開發，並未從產品銷售中產生任何收入，因此已產生重大虧損。本公司預期將持續產生與營運相關的重大研發及一般及行政費用。本公司於 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日的淨虧損分別為 15.3 百萬美元及 62.3 百萬美元，其中包含非營業收入 27.1 百萬美元及非營業虧損 33.4 百萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司累計虧損為 412.3 百萬美元。本公司預期虧損將隨我們持續推進 soquelitinib、ciforadenant 與 mupadolimab 的開發、尋求相關監管批准並開始商業化，以及開發其他產品候選藥物而增加。即使本公司未來實現獲利，也可能無法在隨後期間維持獲利。
自我們成立以來至2025年12月31日，我們主要透過股票的銷售與發行來資助運作，包括2016年3月的首次公開發行（"IPO"）以及隨後的追加公開發行。2024年5月，我們完成一項註冊直接發行，出售我們的普通股、預資 warrants 及普通股 warrants，淨收入約為30.3 百萬美元，加上普通股 warrants 行權所得54.3 百萬美元。
2024年8月6日，我們與Jefferies LLC（"Jefferies"）簽訂一項公開市場銷售協議（"2024銷售協議"），用以出售我們的普通股，不定時進行，總共淨銷售收入最高達100.0 百萬美元，透過一項市場現金股票發行計劃，Jefferies將擔任我們的銷售代理。根據2024銷售協議發行與銷售普通股，被視為根據1933年證券法（已修正）所定義的"市場現金"發行。
依據 1933 年證券交易法（Securities Act of 1933）修正條文發行。Jefferies 有權就其提供的服務，就透過 2024 年銷售協議（2024 Sales Agreement）出售普通股所得的總銷售額中取得最高達 3.0% 的報酬。
在截至2025年12月31日的會計年度內，我們未透過本公司現行的市場現貨發行計畫出售任何普通股，且根據2024年銷售協議，仍有100.0 百萬美元可供出售。
配合本公司於2026年1月進行的跟進公開發行，本公司已針對2024年銷售協議暫停「市場現貨」發行計畫（詳見附註17，後續事件）。
本公司之三項產品候選藥物soquelitinib、ciforadenant及mupadolimab，目前由本公司及/或合作夥伴Angel Pharmaceuticals進行臨牀開發。除中國大陸及香港、澳門地區外，本公司擁有這些產品候選藥物的全球權利。

由於本公司持續進行的開發工作，我們預期未來一段時間內將需要投入大量資源。因此，我們將需要額外資金以支應持續營運。在能夠從產品銷售產生顯著收入之前，若有的話，我們預期將透過公開或私募股權或債務融資或其他來源來籌措資金，這些來源可能包含與第三方的合作。此種融資可能導致股東權益稀釋，並可能包含債務契約及償還義務或其他限制，這些限制可能影響本公司業務。若我們透過戰略合作協議籌措額外資金，我們可能必須放棄對產品候選藥物的寶貴權利，包括潛在的未來收入來源。本公司可能無法在合適的條件下或完全無法取得足夠的額外資金。例如，本公司及其他生物科技公司的股票交易價格因諸如疫情影響、通貨膨脹率或利率上升或廣泛課徵關稅及其他貿易管制等因素而波動極大。因此，我們可能面臨透過銷售本公司普通股籌措資金的困難，且任何銷售可能在不利條件下進行。本公司若無法在需要時籌措資金，將對本公司財務狀況及執行業務策略的能力產生負面影響。我們需要產生顯著收入以實現盈利，但我們可能永遠無法做到。

截至2025年12月31日，本公司擁有約56.8 百萬美元的資金資源，包含現金、現金等價物及市場可交易證券。本公司於2026年1月23日完成一項跟進公開發行，產生約189.4 百萬美元的淨資金。根據目前可用的現金資源及目前預計的營運規模與現金流，我們預期現金資源足夠支應本公司將各項計畫推進至2028年第二季。根據適用的會計準則，本公司評估是否存在條件及事件，整體考量後，可能對本公司持續經營能力產生重大疑慮，至少持續12個月，自本年度報表（包含於本10-K年度報告其他部分）發佈日算起，並結論為本公司現有現金、現金等價物及市場可交易證券，包括約189.4 百萬美元的淨資金（來自2026年1月跟進公開發行），足夠支應本公司至少12個月的營運資金。然而，本公司仍需持續籌措額外資金以支應營運。詳見「風險因素—與本公司有限營運歷史、財務狀況及需額外資金相關的風險」。
本公司目前沒有製造能力，也沒有意圖建立任何製造能力。本公司沒有用以製造產品候選藥物的商業製造設施。因此，本公司依賴第三方根據本公司規格，以足夠數量、準時、符合適當的監管標準且價格具有競爭力的方式供應產品候選藥物。

headings: 與我們有限營運歷史、財務狀況及對額外資金需求相關的風險
與我們產品候選藥物的發現及開發相關的風險
若我們在臨牀試驗中遇到招募受試者困難，我們的臨牀開發活動可能延遲或受到其他不利影響。
我們可能無法成功進行識別或發現額外產品候選藥物的相關努力。
與我們依賴第三方相關的風險
我們依賴第三方執行我們部分或全部製造、研究及臨牀前與臨牀測試工作，這些第三方可能無法順利執行。
我們與合同製造商皆須面對重大監管要求，而我們所依賴的合同製造商可能無法持續符合監管要求。
本公司對第三方之依賴，使我們必須分享我們的商業機密，這會增加競爭對手發現這些機密，或我們的商業機密遭不當使用或揭露之可能性。
產品候選藥物商業化相關風險
若我們未能在所公告及預期的時間內達成預期的開發目標，將可能延宕產品之商業化，進而導致本公司股票價格下跌。
paragraphs: 本公司業務涉及許多重大風險，部分風險已於下文說明。您應謹慎考量下文所述風險與不確定性，並配合本年度10-K財務報告中所有其他資訊，包括我們經審計的合併財務報表及相關附註，以及「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」。若任何上述風險實現，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果與前景造成重大且不利的影響。此外，尚有其他未為本公司所知或目前認為不重要之風險與不確定性，亦可能影響本公司業務營運。
自本公司成立以來，我們已產生重大營運虧損，且預期在可預見的未來仍將產生重大虧損。我們可能永遠無法產生任何收入或實現盈利，或即使實現盈利，也可能無法維持盈利狀態。

本公司為一家臨牀階段生技製藥公司，至今尚未從產品候選藥物銷售中產生收入。生技製藥產品開發屬高度投機性事業，並涉及相當程度的風險。截至目前為止，本公司主要致力於開發領先產品候選藥物，soquelitinib、ciforadenant 以及 mupadolimab，並研究其他產品候選藥物。自本公司於 2014 年 1 月成立以來，已產生顯著的營運虧損，且至今尚未從銷售中產生任何收入。若產品候選藥物未獲批准，本公司可能永遠無法產生任何收入。本公司於 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度、2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度及 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度分別產生淨虧損 15.3 百萬美元、62.3 百萬美元及 27.0 百萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司累計虧損為 412.3 百萬美元。本公司預期將持續產生虧損，且在持續進行產品候選藥物開發、尋求監管批准以及若獲批准後開始商業化 soquelitinib，以及開發其他產品候選藥物的過程中，這些虧損將會增加。即使本公司未來達成獲利，也可能無法在隨後期間維持獲利。本公司過去的虧損，加上預期未來的虧損，已對本公司股東權益及營運成果產生及將持續產生負面影響。
我們將需要大量額外資金以實現目標，若無法在需要時以可接受的條件或完全無法取得必要資金，將迫使我們延遲、限制、減少或終止產品開發、其他營運或商業化工作。

自本公司成立以來，我們的大部分努力都集中在soquelitinib、ciforadenant與mupadolimab之研究與開發上。我們認為，在可預見的未來，我們仍將投入大量資源，以持續進行soquelitinib之臨牀開發、尋求監管批准，以及若獲批准則準備商業化，以及進行其他開發計畫中的產品候選藥物。這些支出將包括研究與開發費用、進行非臨牀研究與臨牀試驗、取得監管批准、製造與供應、銷售與行銷及一般營運費用。此外，其他未預期的費用也可能產生。由於任何臨牀試驗及/或監管批准程序的結果極為不確定，我們可能無法準確預估完成soquelitinib、ciforadenant與mupadolimab或其他產品候選藥物之開發、監管批准程序與商業化所需的實際金額。
